about: Built by tools/build_subforce.py. The building, the pier, the Nautilus, the lawn, the plaza and the parking lot are traced from OpenStreetMap, true to scale, and turned 16° so the museum front runs left to right (up is north-north-west). The Navy publishes no floor plan, so the rooms inside the museum are placed from visitors’ descriptions and are approximate. The Nautilus is a diagram of the compartments on the tour.
source: OpenStreetMap (building, pier, Nautilus, grounds); visitors’ descriptions of the galleries; rooms inside approximate
units: metres x 4, turned 16° (up is north-north-west); the Nautilus floor is a diagram

floors.label: Museum · Grounds
floors.area: Entrance · Lobby · Main Gallery · Control Room · periscopes · outdoor submarines · the Nautilus pier

rooms.name: Lobby: the docent desk (free scavenger hunt for children), restrooms, and Jules Verne’s Nautilus hanging just inside the doors
Museum Store (run by the Submarine Force Library & Museum Association): submarine and Connecticut gifts; the way out goes through it
Theater (about 80 seats): a film on submarine history plays on a loop
rooms.label: Theater

rooms.name: Today’s Submarine Force: modern submarines, what they do and how the Submarine Force is organised
rooms.label: Today

rooms.name: Main Hallway: the cutaway model of a modern submarine and the wall of submarine models, all to one scale, from the Holland to the Columbia class
rooms.label: Hallway

rooms.name: Control Room: the real control center of USS Sturgeon (SSN-637); take the controls and try steering a submarine
rooms.label: Control

rooms.name: Attack Center: three working periscopes through the roof; look at the Nautilus, the Thames and the Coast Guard Academy across the river
rooms.label: Periscopes

rooms.name: Main Gallery (two storeys high): Bushnell’s Turtle, the big Gato model, the McCann rescue chamber, torpedoes, the Polaris missile and the history of the U.S. Submarine Force
rooms.label: Main Gallery

rooms.name: Walk to the main entrance, under the two hull rings
Front lawn: the Japanese HA-8 and the U.S. X-1 midget submarines, a swimmer delivery vehicle, sections of the NR-1, a deck gun and the Harpoon missile at the door
rooms.label: Lawn

rooms.name: Free parking (gates are locked after closing time); picnic tables at the far end of the lot
Memorial Plaza: the sail of USS George Washington (SSBN-598), the Nautilus propellers and the 41 for Freedom memorial
rooms.label: Plaza

rooms.name: Railroad tracks (Providence and Worcester freight line)
Railroad tracks: cross only on the walkway
Walkway from the museum to the pier, across the railroad
Nautilus Pier: at the small pier house a sailor on duty hands out the audio-tour wands
Brow (gangway) onto the Nautilus
Historic Ship Nautilus (SSN-571), the first nuclear-powered submarine: a self-guided audio tour of the forward compartments, about 30 minutes (see the Nautilus floor)
rooms.label: Nautilus
